title: त्रिपञ्चाशदधिकद्विशततमोऽध्यायः
titleEn: Adhyaya 253 · Jajali and the weigher Tuladhara

summary.en: Bhishma tells the old story of the ascetic Jajali, who stood so long in the forest that birds nested in his matted hair and, proud of his austerity, thought himself the equal of any. A voice told him that the merchant Tuladhara of Varanasi was more learned in dharma than he.
summary.kn: ಕಾಡಿನಲ್ಲಿ ಬಹುಕಾಲ ನಿಂತು ಜಟೆಯಲ್ಲಿ ಹಕ್ಕಿಗಳು ಗೂಡು ಕಟ್ಟಿದ ತಪಸ್ವಿ ಜಾಜಲಿ ತನ್ನ ತಪಸ್ಸಿನ ಹೆಮ್ಮೆಯಲ್ಲಿ ಯಾರಿಗೂ ಕಡಿಮೆಯಲ್ಲವೆಂದು ತಿಳಿದ ಹಳೆಯ ಕಥೆಯನ್ನು ಭೀಷ್ಮ ಹೇಳುತ್ತಾನೆ. ವಾರಾಣಸಿಯ ವರ್ತಕ ತುಲಾಧಾರ ಅವನಿಗಿಂತ ಧರ್ಮದಲ್ಲಿ ಹೆಚ್ಚು ತಿಳಿದವನೆಂದು ಒಂದು ಧ್ವನಿ ಹೇಳಿತು.
summary.hi: भीष्म तपस्वी जाजलि की पुरानी कथा कहते हैं जो वन में इतना खड़ा रहा कि उसकी जटाओं में पक्षियों ने घोंसले बना लिए और वह तप के गर्व में स्वयं को किसी से कम न मानने लगा। एक वाणी ने कहा कि वाराणसी का व्यापारी तुलाधार धर्म में उससे अधिक जानकार है।
summary.te: అడవిలో చాలాకాలం నిలబడి జటల్లో పక్షులు గూళ్లు కట్టిన తపస్వి జాజలి తన తపస్సు గర్వంతో తాను ఎవరికీ తీసిపోనని భావించిన పాత కథను భీష్ముడు చెబుతాడు. వారణాసి వ్యాపారి తులాధారుడు అతని కంటే ధర్మంలో ఎక్కువ తెలిసినవాడని ఒక వాణి చెప్పింది.
summary.ta: காட்டில் நீண்டநாள் நின்றதால் சடையில் பறவைகள் கூடு கட்டிய தவசி ஜாஜலி, தவச் செருக்கில் தன்னை யாருக்கும் குறைந்தவனல்ல என்று எண்ணிய பழைய கதையைப் பீஷ்மர் கூறுகிறார். வாரணாசி வணிகன் துலாதாரன் தர்மத்தில் அவனை விட அறிந்தவன் என்று ஒரு குரல் கூறியது.
summary.ml: തപസ്വിയായ ജാജലി വനത്തിൽ വളരെനേരം നിന്നതുകൊണ്ട് ജടയിൽ പക്ഷികൾ കൂടുകൂട്ടിയതും, തപസ്സിൽ അഹങ്കരിച്ച് താനാണ് എല്ലാവർക്കും തുല്യനെന്ന് കരുതിയതുമായ പഴയ കഥ ഭീഷ്മർ പറയുന്നു. വാരാണസിയിലെ വ്യാപാരിയായ തുലാധരൻ ധർമ്മത്തിൽ തന്നെക്കാൾ പണ്ഡിതനാണെന്ന് ഒരു ശബ്ദം അദ്ദേഹത്തോട് പറയുന്നു.

source: Mahabharata, Critical Edition (BORI, Pune) 12.253; e-text by M. Tokunaga and J. D. Smith, © BORI 1999, version of Wed Jun 16 2021

verses.text: भीष्म उवाच

meaning.en: Bhishma said:

verses.text:
अत्राप्युदाहरन्तीममितिहासं पुरातनम् ।
तुलाधारस्य वाक्यानि धर्मे जाजलिना सह ॥

meaning.en: On this too they tell an ancient story: the words of Tuladhara to Jajali on dharma.

verses.text:
वने वनचरः कश्चिज्जाजलिर्नाम वै द्विजः ।
सागरोद्देशमागम्य तपस्तेपे महातपाः ॥

meaning.en: In the forest there was a brahmin of the woods named Jajali, who came to the seashore and practised great austerity.

verses.text:
नियतो नियताहारश्चीराजिनजटाधरः ।
मलपङ्कधरो धीमान्बहून्वर्षगणान्मुनिः ॥

meaning.en: Disciplined, disciplined in food, wearing bark, antelope skin and matted hair, bearing dirt and mud, the wise sage did so for many years.

verses.text:
स कदाचिन्महातेजा जलवासो महीपते ।
चचार लोकान्विप्रर्षिः प्रेक्षमाणो मनोजवः ॥

meaning.en: Once, king, that radiant brahmin sage, living in the water, travelled the worlds, quick as thought, looking about.

verses.text:
स चिन्तयामास मुनिर्जलमध्ये कदाचन ।
विप्रेक्ष्य सागरान्तां वै महीं सवनकाननाम् ॥

meaning.en: Once, in the midst of the water, the sage, looking at the earth bounded by the sea with its forests and groves, thought:

verses.text:
न मया सदृशोऽस्तीह लोके स्थावरजङ्गमे ।
अप्सु वैहायसं गच्छेन्मया योऽन्यः सहेति वै ॥

meaning.en: "There is no one in the world like me, among the moving and unmoving; who else could go with me through the water or through the sky?"

verses.text:
स दृश्यमानो रक्षोभिर्जलमध्येऽवदत्ततः ।
अब्रुवंश्च पिशाचास्तं नैवं त्वं वक्तुमर्हसि ॥

meaning.en: Seen by rakshasas in the water, he said this, and the pishachas told him, "You should not speak so.

verses.text:
तुलाधारो वणिग्धर्मा वाराणस्यां महायशाः ।
सोऽप्येवं नार्हते वक्तुं यथा त्वं द्विजसत्तम ॥

meaning.en: Tuladhara, of the merchant's dharma, famous, in Varanasi, does not say such a thing as you, best of brahmins."

verses.text:
इत्युक्तो जाजलिर्भूतैः प्रत्युवाच महातपाः ।
पश्येयं तमहं प्राज्ञं तुलाधारं यशस्विनम् ॥

meaning.en: Thus addressed by the spirits, the very austere Jajali replied: "I would like to see that wise and renowned Tuladhara."

verses.text:
इति ब्रुवाणं तमृषिं रक्षांस्युद्धृत्य सागरात् ।
अब्रुवन्गच्छ पन्थानमास्थायेमं द्विजोत्तम ॥

meaning.en: As the sage said so, the rakshasas lifted him out of the sea and said, "Go, best of brahmins, by this road."

verses.text:
इत्युक्तो जाजलिर्भूतैर्जगाम विमनास्तदा ।
वाराणस्यां तुलाधारं समासाद्याब्रवीद्वचः ॥

meaning.en: So addressed by the spirits, Jajali went, downcast, and reaching Tuladhara in Varanasi, spoke to him.

verses.text: युधिष्ठिर उवाच

meaning.en: Yudhishthira said:

verses.text:
किं कृतं सुकृतं कर्म तात जाजलिना पुरा ।
येन सिद्धिं परां प्राप्तस्तन्नो व्याख्यातुमर्हसि ॥

meaning.en: What good deed did Jajali do before, grandfather, by which he reached high success? Please explain this to us.

verses.text: भीष्म उवाच

meaning.en: Bhishma said:

verses.text:
अतीव तपसा युक्तो घोरेण स बभूव ह ।
नद्युपस्पर्शनरतः सायं प्रातर्महातपाः ॥

meaning.en: He became exceedingly devoted to terrible austerity, delighting in bathing in the river morning and evening, a great ascetic.

verses.text:
अग्नीन्परिचरन्सम्यक्स्वाध्यायपरमो द्विजः ।
वानप्रस्थविधानज्ञो जाजलिर्ज्वलितः श्रिया ॥

meaning.en: That brahmin, tending the fires properly and devoted to Vedic recitation, knowing the rules of the forest-dweller, Jajali, blazed with splendour.

verses.text:
सत्ये तपसि तिष्ठन्स न च धर्ममवैक्षत ।
वर्षास्वाकाशशायी स हेमन्ते जलसंश्रयः ॥

meaning.en: Standing in truth and austerity, he did not look to dharma. In the rains he lay in the open, in winter he stayed in water,

verses.text:
वातातपसहो ग्रीष्मे न च धर्ममविन्दत ।
दुःखशय्याश्च विविधा भूमौ च परिवर्तनम् ॥

meaning.en: in summer he endured wind and sun; yet he did not find dharma. He suffered painful beds of many kinds and rolled on the ground.

verses.text:
ततः कदाचित्स मुनिर्वर्षास्वाकाशमास्थितः ।
अन्तरिक्षाज्जलं मूर्ध्ना प्रत्यगृह्णान्मुहुर्मुहुः ॥

meaning.en: Once, as the sage stood in the open in the rainy season, he again and again caught the water from the sky on his head.

verses.text:
अथ तस्य जटाः क्लिन्ना बभूवुर्ग्रथिताः प्रभो ।
अरण्यगमनान्नित्यं मलिनो मलसंयुताः ॥

meaning.en: Then his matted locks, my lord, became wet and tangled, dirty from constant wandering in the forest.

verses.text:
स कदाचिन्निराहारो वायुभक्षो महातपाः ।
तस्थौ काष्ठवदव्यग्रो न चचाल च कर्हिचित् ॥

meaning.en: Once the great ascetic, fasting and living on air, stood like a log, undisturbed, and never moved.

verses.text:
तस्य स्म स्थाणुभूतस्य निर्विचेष्टस्य भारत ।
कुलिङ्गशकुनौ राजन्नीडं शिरसि चक्रतुः ॥

meaning.en: As he stood like a post, motionless, Bharata, a pair of kulinga birds made a nest on his head.

verses.text:
स तौ दयावान्विप्रर्षिरुपप्रैक्षत दम्पती ।
कुर्वाणं नीडकं तत्र जटासु तृणतन्तुभिः ॥

meaning.en: The compassionate brahmin sage watched the couple making their nest in his locks with grass and threads.

verses.text:
यदा स न चलत्येव स्थाणुभूतो महातपाः ।
ततस्तौ परिविश्वस्तौ सुखं तत्रोषतुस्तदा ॥

meaning.en: Since the great ascetic did not move at all, standing like a post, the two grew trusting and lived there happily.

verses.text:
अतीतास्वथ वर्षासु शरत्काल उपस्थिते ।
प्राजापत्येन विधिना विश्वासात्काममोहितौ ॥

meaning.en: When the rains had passed and autumn came, the two birds, trusting him and carried away by desire, according to the rule of Prajapati,

verses.text:
तत्रापातयतां राजञ्शिरस्यण्डानि खेचरौ ।
तान्यबुध्यत तेजस्वी स विप्रः संशितव्रतः ॥

meaning.en: dropped eggs on his head, king. The radiant brahmin of strict vows noticed them.

verses.text:
बुद्ध्वा च स महातेजा न चचालैव जाजलिः ।
धर्मे धृतमना नित्यं नाधर्मं स त्वरोचयत् ॥

meaning.en: Though he knew, the very radiant Jajali did not move; his mind was always set on dharma, and he did not like adharma.

verses.text:
अहन्यहनि चागम्य ततस्तौ तस्य मूर्धनि ।
आश्वासितौ वै वसतः संप्रहृष्टौ तदा विभो ॥

meaning.en: Day after day the two came to his head and lived there reassured and delighted.

verses.text:
अण्डेभ्यस्त्वथ पुष्टेभ्यः प्रजायन्त शकुन्तकाः ।
व्यवर्धन्त च तत्रैव न चाकम्पत जाजलिः ॥

meaning.en: From the nourished eggs fledglings were born, and they grew there, and Jajali did not stir.

verses.text:
स रक्षमाणस्त्वण्डानि कुलिङ्गानां यतव्रतः ।
तथैव तस्थौ धर्मात्मा निर्विचेष्टः समाहितः ॥

meaning.en: Guarding the kulinga eggs, the disciplined and righteous one stood so, motionless and composed.

verses.text:
ततस्तु कालसमये बभूवुस्तेऽथ पक्षिणः ।
बुबुधे तांश्च स मुनिर्जातपक्षाञ्शकुन्तकान् ॥

meaning.en: Then in time the birds were born, and the sage knew the fledglings had grown wings.

verses.text:
ततः कदाचित्तांस्तत्र पश्यन्पक्षीन्यतव्रतः ।
बभूव परमप्रीतस्तदा मतिमतां वरः ॥

meaning.en: Then once, seeing those birds there, the disciplined one, best of the wise, was exceedingly pleased.

verses.text:
तथा तानभिसंवृद्धान्दृष्ट्वा चाप्नुवतां मुदम् ।
शकुनौ निर्भयौ तत्र ऊषतुश्चात्मजैः सह ॥

meaning.en: Seeing them grown and happy, the two birds lived there fearless with their young.

verses.text:
जातपक्षांश्च सोऽपश्यदुड्डीनान्पुनरागतान् ।
सायं सायं द्विजान्विप्रो न चाकम्पत जाजलिः ॥

meaning.en: He saw them with wings, fly off and return; the brahmin, evening after evening, did not stir.

verses.text:
कदाचित्पुनरभ्येत्य पुनर्गच्छन्ति संततम् ।
त्यक्ता मातृपितृभ्यां ते न चाकम्पत जाजलिः ॥

meaning.en: Sometimes they came back and again went away, again and again; abandoned by mother and father, they did so, and Jajali did not move.

verses.text:
अथ ते दिवसं चारीं गत्वा सायं पुनर्नृप ।
उपावर्तन्त तत्रैव निवासार्थं शकुन्तकाः ॥

meaning.en: Then the birds, having gone a day's range, returned there in the evening to stay.

verses.text:
कदाचिद्दिवसान्पञ्च समुत्पत्य विहंगमाः ।
षष्ठेऽहनि समाजग्मुर्न चाकम्पत जाजलिः ॥

meaning.en: Sometimes the birds would fly off for five days and return on the sixth; Jajali did not stir.

verses.text:
क्रमेण च पुनः सर्वे दिवसानि बहून्यपि ।
नोपावर्तन्त शकुना जातप्राणाः स्म ते यदा ॥

meaning.en: Gradually all the birds, for many days, no longer came back when they had grown strong.

verses.text:
कदाचिन्मासमात्रेण समुत्पत्य विहंगमाः ।
नैवागच्छंस्ततो राजन्प्रातिष्ठत स जाजलिः ॥

meaning.en: Once the birds flew away for a whole month and did not come back, king, so Jajali moved off.

verses.text:
ततस्तेषु प्रलीनेषु जाजलिर्जातविस्मयः ।
सिद्धोऽस्मीति मतिं चक्रे ततस्तं मान आविशत् ॥

meaning.en: When they had gone, Jajali was amazed and thought, "I am perfected," and then pride entered him.

verses.text:
स तथा निर्गतान्दृष्ट्वा शकुन्तान्नियतव्रतः ।
संभावितात्मा संभाव्य भृशं प्रीतस्तदाभवन् ॥

meaning.en: Seeing the birds gone out so, the disciplined and self-regarding one, having thought well of himself, was very pleased.

verses.text:
स नद्यां समुपस्पृश्य तर्पयित्वा हुताशनम् ।
उदयन्तमथादित्यमभ्यगच्छन्महातपाः ॥

meaning.en: Having bathed in the river and satisfied the fire, the great ascetic went toward the rising sun.

verses.text:
संभाव्य चटकान्मूर्ध्नि जाजलिर्जपतां वरः ।
आस्फोटयत्तदाकाशे धर्मः प्राप्तो मयेति वै ॥

meaning.en: Thinking well of the sparrows on his head, Jajali, best of those who recite, slapped his arms in the sky and said, "I have attained dharma!"

verses.text:
अथान्तरिक्षे वागासीत्तां स शुश्राव जाजलिः ।
धर्मेण न समस्त्वं वै तुलाधारस्य जाजले ॥

meaning.en: Then a voice in the sky spoke, and Jajali heard it: "Jajali, you are not equal to Tuladhara in dharma."

verses.text:
वाराणस्यां महाप्राज्ञस्तुलाधारः प्रतिष्ठितः ।
सोऽप्येवं नार्हते वक्तुं यथा त्वं भाषसे द्विज ॥

meaning.en: "The very wise Tuladhara is established in Varanasi; he too does not speak as you speak, brahmin."

verses.text:
सोऽमर्षवशमापन्नस्तुलाधारदिदृक्षया ।
पृथिवीमचरद्राजन्यत्रसायंगृहो मुनिः ॥

meaning.en: Overcome by impatience, wishing to see Tuladhara, the sage wandered the earth, stopping where evening found him.

verses.text:
कालेन महतागच्छत्स तु वाराणसीं पुरीम् ।
विक्रीणन्तं च पण्यानि तुलाधारं ददर्श सः ॥

meaning.en: After a long time he came to the city of Varanasi, and there he saw Tuladhara selling his wares.

verses.text:
सोऽपि दृष्ट्वैव तं विप्रमायान्तं भाण्डजीवनः ।
समुत्थाय सुसंहृष्टः स्वागतेनाभ्यपूजयत् ॥

meaning.en: Seeing the brahmin coming, the shopkeeper rose, very glad, and honoured him with a welcome.

verses.text: तुलाधार उवाच

meaning.en: Tuladhara said:

verses.text:
आयानेवासि विदितो मम ब्रह्मन्न संशयः ।
ब्रवीमि यत्तु वचनं तच्छृणुष्व द्विजोत्तम ॥

meaning.en: Brahmin, I knew you were coming, without doubt. Hear, best of brahmins, what I say.

verses.text:
सागरानूपमाश्रित्य तपस्तप्तं त्वया महत् ।
न च धर्मस्य संज्ञां त्वं पुरा वेत्थ कथंचन ॥

meaning.en: You practised great austerity by the seashore, but you did not know the name of dharma before.

verses.text:
ततः सिद्धस्य तपसा तव विप्र शकुन्तकाः ।
क्षिप्रं शिरस्यजायन्त ते च संभावितास्त्वया ॥

meaning.en: Then, brahmin, perfected by your austerity, birds were soon born on your head, and you thought well of them.

verses.text:
जातपक्षा यदा ते च गताश्चारीमितस्ततः ।
मन्यमानस्ततो धर्मं चटकप्रभवं द्विज ।
खे वाचं त्वमथाश्रौषीर्मां प्रति द्विजसत्तम ॥

meaning.en: When they had wings and went off on their daily rounds here and there, thinking dharma had come from the sparrows, brahmin, you then heard a voice in the sky about me, best of brahmins.

verses.text:
अमर्षवशमापन्नस्ततः प्राप्तो भवानिह ।
करवाणि प्रियं किं ते तद्ब्रूहि द्विजसत्तम ॥

meaning.en: Overcome by impatience, you have come here. What can I do that is dear to you? Tell me, best of brahmins.
